# Investigation: Abnormal number of password retrievals for this user (4cc3c489-4c77-4cfd-9f22-a0561136c6ce)

**Verdict:** Confirmed threat (coordinated) — escalate
**Confidence:** High
**Primary entity / pivot:** external IP 198.51.100.57
**MITRE ATT&CK:** T1078, T1003, T1133, T1098, T1071, T1213
**Analyst action taken:** case escalation recommended (dry-run: no write executed)
**Taxonomy outcome:** raised

## What fired
A system-generated CRITICAL alert (riskScore 99) aggregating abnormal CyberArk PAM password retrievals and first-time logins across ~820 users. Per-detection counts are tiny (e.g. "abnormal (4) of password retrievals for paul.thomas17954"), so the aggregate size alone is not the signal.

## Evidence
- Threat summary named a single external IP 198.51.100.57 tying the activity together — *(source: exabeam_threat_summary)*
- IP pivot: src_ip 198.51.100.57 appears as the source of vpn-login (F5) and endpoint-login (Windows Security) events for many distinct users (daniel.rodriguez, paul.thomas, lucas.white, ...) — a single source IP across many distinct users — *(source: exabeam_search_events)*
- Representative user paul.thomas17954: 4 CyberArk PAM password-checkout events, every one sourced from 198.51.100.57 — CyberArk PAM password-checkout events tied to that IP — plus an http-session from the same IP — *(source: exabeam_search_events)*
- VPN + endpoint logins for many users from the same IP corroborate a coordinated push, not 800 coincidences.

## Assessment
**Malicious hypothesis:** one external host (198.51.100.57) is using/harvesting credentials to authenticate as many users — PAM vault checkouts, first-time logins, endpoint logins. Supported by the shared source IP across VPN, endpoint, PAM, and web events for unrelated users.
**Benign hypothesis:** a shared jump host / NAT egress. Contradicted by the interactive activity mix across many human users; no positive benign explanation found.
**Deciding evidence:** the single source IP 198.51.100.57 appearing across password-checkouts and endpoint/VPN logins for many distinct users.

## Verdict & rationale
Coordinated credential-access campaign. The big user count was not the signal; the shared source IP was. A positive benign explanation was actively sought and not found, so this is not a false positive, and its scale makes it a human-owned escalation rather than an auto-close.

## Actions
- Recommended: exabeam_create_case to escalate, then exabeam_create_case_notes to document (not executed in this dry-run).
- **Recommended containment (analyst to approve in EDR/IAM):** block 198.51.100.57 at the VPN/edge; disable / force-reauth accounts seen from it; rotate credentials retrieved from the affected CyberArk safes (e.g. USER6403).
- Did NOT dismiss or close — this is the opposite of a false positive.
